title: 1999 AHSME Problem 7
statement: What is the largest number of acute angles that a convex hexagon can have?

solutions.text:
Each acute interior angle corresponds to an exterior angle greater than \(90^\circ.\) Since the exterior angles of a convex polygon sum to \(360^\circ,\) at most three of them can exceed \(90^\circ.\) This bound is attainable: take a hexagon with equal side lengths and exterior angles alternating \(100^\circ\) and \(20^\circ.\) Its edge directions split into two triples \(120^\circ\) apart, so it closes, and its interior angles alternate between \(80^\circ\) and \(160^\circ.\) Hence the largest possible number is three.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The exterior angles of a convex polygon sum to \(360^\circ\)
An acute interior angle gives an exterior angle greater than \(90^\circ\)
